summary: PAPER-HE-LI-SHI-ETAL-23 extracts He–Li–Shi–Yang, A proof of the Kudla–Rapoport conjecture for Krämer models (Invent. Math. 234 (2023) 721–817). It has 46 items (3 planned, 43 missing), three routes and 30 source issues, after a thorough review that found E7/E8, a gap in the proof of the main theorem. Its statuses hold, including S.6/S.7 after RS-18, and both Part IIs coalesce consistently with five other extractions. One finding, medium. Seven findings affect a stated result, among them E7. All seven were read against the authors' final version and arXiv v2, and the file has no sourceVersions. The collation worklist that §18 relies on to send such findings to the version of record does not list this paper: scripts/collation.py's journal pattern fails on 'Inventiones Mathematicae', and papers.json links only the author's homepage. The same pattern hides seven more Inventiones and Acta papers, with 53 stated findings in all. Fix: add sourceVersions here, correct the papers.json entry, and ask the maintainer to fix the pattern.
checked: Independence: the extraction is by Claude Code cc-fb70e5 (issue #1237) and its review by Claude Code cc-442dc5. This worker (Claude Code, cc-c2c06b) did neither. My earlier review of the RS-18 red team concerns the SchemeKTheoryOperations stages cited here only as planners.

Read the three routes, their reasons and briefs, and the statuses of all 46 items in the repository at 0aab28ff. All five cited stage ids exist in the assembled atlas (2840 stages, 8007 edges). S.6 and S.7 were narrowed by RS-18, accepted before this review. They still keep 'extension of K.7 external products to schemes/supports' and 'the K/G realization …, scheme gamma filtration and regular-scheme Chow comparison', so item 10 (K-groups with supports and the codimension filtration) stays planned. AL.0 (item 20), QM.0 (item 29, the q-binomial theorem, which neither library has) and GN.3 (route 3) are unchanged.

The two Part IIs: UnitaryKudlaRapoportCycles (parent GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights) and UnitaryRapoportZinkSpacesAndRSZModels (parent PELModuli) are shared under identical ids and titles by LI-ZHANG-22-B, LI-LIU-21, LI-LIU-22, ZHANG-21 and LIU-ETAL-22. Both titles reproduce their parents' current titles. The local-density items at GN.3 match how PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24 routes its Hermitian local densities.

Source issues: checked how the stated-result findings are recorded (finding 1). I did not re-verify E1–E30 mathematically. The review checked them with 273 direct density computations, n ≤ 9 checks of Theorem 7.1 and finite-field counts, and re-derived the Lemma 9.6 obstruction behind E7 and E8. Crossref (doi 10.1007/s00222-023-01209-1) records no correction.

Collation tooling: evaluated scripts/collation.py's provenance(), stated() and published_exists() on this record and on every papers.json entry. This found the eight papers whose version of record is missed because of the Invent/Acta/Mathematica pattern. Five other listed papers that are genuinely arXiv-only are correctly excluded.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-HE-LI-SHI-ETAL-23.result.json: top level (no sourceVersions) and sourceIssues E1, E2, E7, E9, E14, E23, E24 (affects 'a stated result'); research/blueprint/papers/papers.json entry PAPER-HE-LI-SHI-ETAL-23 (citation 'Inventiones Mathematicae (2023)', link to the author's homepage); scripts/collation.py JOURNAL pattern
findings.claim: Seven of this extraction's 30 source issues affect a stated result: E1, E2, E7, E9, E14, E23 and E24. E7 says Lemma 9.6 is false in a configuration where it leaves a gap in the proof of the main theorem. All seven were read against the authors' final version on Chao Li's homepage and arXiv v2, not the Invent. Math. version of record, and the file has no sourceVersions. §18's safeguard for this case is the collation worklist (scripts/collation.py, with collation jobs), which is meant to find papers 'whose quoted statements still rest on a preprint'. It does not list this paper. published_exists() judges from papers.json whether a version of record exists. This entry links to the author's homepage, not a publisher, and its citation reads 'Inventiones Mathematicae (2023)'. The JOURNAL pattern requires a word boundary after 'Invent' and lists only 'Math(ematische|ematics|\.)', so it matches neither 'Inventiones' nor 'Mathematicae'. The tool therefore decides no published version exists and silently drops all seven findings. The same regex hides three other Inventiones papers (LI-ZHANG-22, CLAUSEN-MATHEW-21, CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18) and four in Acta Mathematica, where 'Acta' is not a listed journal and 'Mathematica' matches nothing (ESNAULT-GROECHENIG-20, NELSON-VENKATESH-21, NIKOLAUS-SCHOLZE-18, KOYMANS-PAGANO). Together these carry 53 stated-result findings.
findings.evidence: scripts/collation.py: JOURNAL = re.compile(r"(Ann(als|\.)|Invent|J\.|Journal|Publ|Duke|Compositio|Forum|Bull|Proc|Trans|IH[ÉE]S|Math(ematische|ematics|\.)|Algebra|Geometry|Topology|Crelle|Astérisque)\b.{0,40}\(?(19|20)\d\d", re.I). published_exists() returns bool(JOURNAL.search(citation)) when the link is not a publisher host. Evaluated at this revision: for the papers.json entry {'id': 'PAPER-HE-LI-SHI-ETAL-23', 'citation': 'He–Li–Shi–Yang, "A proof of Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for Krämer models", Inventiones Mathematicae (2023)', 'link': 'https://www.math.columbia.edu/~chaoli/'}, collation.published_exists(...) is False, collation.provenance(result) is 'preprint', and collation.stated(result) returns E1, E2, E7, E9, E14, E23, E24. `python3 scripts/collation.py` lists 70 exposed papers and omits this one. The extraction's readSections: 'the authors' final version, https://www.math.columbia.edu/~chaoli/Kramer.pdf, dated 21 July 2023 … SHA-256 a29d2820…' plus arXiv v2. source.doi 10.1007/s00222-023-01209-1 (Invent. Math. 234 (2023) 721–817). `'sourceVersions' in result` is False. Running the same test over all papers.json entries, eight papers with a journal version of record and stated findings are missed only because of the Invent/Acta/Mathematica pattern: the four Inventiones and four Acta papers named above, with 53 stated findings together.
